newsitem.title: UK: Brent crude prospects brighter as cargoes find hom.
newsitem.headline: Brent crude prospects brighter as cargoes find hom.

text.p: Brent crude held a 45 cent discount to December paper early in the day and the market largely discounted a later inter-affiliate deal at Dec -48 cents, traders said.

Physical Brent's prospects brightened with talk that some two million barrels of the North Sea benchmark were likely to head to the U.S. market after a trader holding the cargoes booked a VLCC for December 3.
The CFD market for next week's dates perked up with a rumoured deal of Nov 25-29 dates at Jan +15 cents, up seven cents from morning levels.
Jan Brent outright values were talked around screen levels of $22.75 the late afternoon but none traded. Intermonth spreads firmed with Dec/Jan gaining four cents to trade at +55 cents.

Two early December Brent cargoes traded at Dec Brent -45 cents in the morning, with the same trader involved as a buyer and seller in both deals. An inter-affiliate deal saw Brent trade down at -48 cents.
Of the three Brent dates which turned wet on Thursday -- including two deferred from the previous day -- two were kept and one was in dispute.

Other North Sea crudes also found homes on Thursday but differentials were weak. A cargo of Forties for Dec 7-9 was sold at Dated Brent +15/+18, down at least two cents on last done. Ekofisk loading Dec 1-3 traded at a three cent premium to Dated Brent while Statfjord and Dragon traded at Dated Brent +8.

In the Med, Urals has moved steadily at recent firm levels of a 57-58 cents discount to Dated Brent, supported by good refining margins, fears of a supply shortage from either weather or maintenance related delays at Novorossiisk and a noticeable dearth of Iranian supplies on the spot market.
